title: Introduce retrospective SLO replay service and cost-attenuation proxy
text:
Introduce retrospective SLO replay service and cost-attenuation proxy

description:
Motivation: We need a low-risk way to evaluate the SLO and cost impact of routing, batching and fallback policy changes against historical traffic slices without touching production runtime. This PR adds a lightweight retrospective SLO replay service (slo-replay) that replays sampled invocation traces against a ruleset engine and the same cost estimator used by the billing pipeline. The goal is to produce per-route SLO impact projections and a cost-attenuation proxy metric that observability rules can use to moderate alert sensitivity during transient rollout experiments.

What this PR does (summary): adds a new slo-replay microservice, a replay job scheduler, an adapter that feeds sampled invocations to the routing policy simulator, a cost-attenuation proxy metric emitted to the observability pipeline, a Grafana dashboard for projected-SLO vs observed-SLO scatter, and alert rule updates to use the attenuation proxy for temporary suppression during canaries.

Key design points: the replay runs offline against anonymized, sampled traces (existing sampled-context export). It uses the same token-cost and kernel-latency model that billing uses to estimate per-invocation cost and per-stage latency. Replay results are aggregated into a time-bucketed projection index keyed by route, model-version, and policy-id. The attenuation proxy is a decayed ratio (projected_error_rate / baseline_error_rate) clipped to [0,2] and emitted as a numeric label so alert rules can multiply thresholds by 1 + attenuation_factor * alpha. The service exposes a small REST status endpoint and writes projection snapshots to the telemetry tier for query.

Checklist: [x] MVP replay engine and rules simulator; [x] emit attenuation proxy metric (telemetry exporter); [x] Grafana dashboard JSON and dashboard provisioning; [x] e2e integration tests for replay -> telemetry pipeline; [x] docs: observability runbook and how-to for canaries; [x] unit tests for policy simulator.

Commits (high level): - 1a2b3c4: initial slo-replay service scaffold and job runner - 2d3e4f5: policy simulator + unit tests, tie into existing sampled-context export - 3f4g5h6: telemetry exporter for attenuation proxy + protobuf schema + index writer - 4h5i6j7: grafana dashboard panels + alert rule changes and runbook docs - 5j6k7l8: test harness and CI adjustments for e2e tests

Files changed (representative): - observability/slo_replay/service.py (new): replay scheduler, adapter to policy simulator - observability/slo_replay/simulator.py (new): deterministic policy simulator with unit tests - telemetry/exporters/attenuation_exporter.go (new): emits attenuation proxy metric with labels - dashboards/provisioning/retro-slo-projections.json (new): Grafana dashboard panels and templates - monitoring/alerting/canary_rules.yaml (modified): use attenuation proxy to suppress noisy alerts - tests/e2e/test_slo_replay_end2end.py (new): end-to-end replay smoke test - docs/observability/slo-replay.md (new): runbook and how-to

Migration and runtime safety: the replay runs only on an offline batch pool with a configurable retention window; default retention is 7 days of sampled contexts. Telemetry emission is rate-limited and namespaced under telemetry.replay to avoid collision with production metrics. The attenuation proxy is advisory by default (alert rules use a conservative alpha=0.25 until we reach 7-day stability in production projections).

Operational notes: added a small sampler config to sampled-context-export so we can increase sampling ratio for short windows when validating new policies. The replay scheduler includes a backfill mode to rerun a specific date range for re-eval.

Why this is different from existing tooling: other efforts run small synthetic replays or ad-hoc notebooks. This PR provides a repeatable, indexable, production-alike replay path with metrics surfaced in dashboards and a formalized attenuation signal that alerting rules can safely consult during rollouts.

Risks and mitigations: - Risk: attenuation proxy could be abused to mask real regressions. Mitigation: default alpha small, audit log for attenuation-enabled alerts, and gating via RBAC on who can flip advisory mode. - Risk: projection model divergence from actual runtime. Mitigation: we log a calibration delta (projection vs observed) and auto-escalate if delta exceeds threshold for 3 windows.

Next steps: collect 2 weeks of replay projections for high-volume routes, evaluate calibration, and iterate alpha per-team.


review_conversation:
Aiden Wu: Overall looks solid. Two concerns: 1) ensure replay doesn't pull unredacted PII; 2) make attenuation labels low-cardinality. Please add a note to runbook and a scrubber step.
Sofia Martinez: Thanks — added a scrubber in sampled-context export and a config flag (redaction_policy) in service.py. Also switched attenuation labels to coarse enums (low/medium/high) plus a numeric factor for fine-grained calculation.
Priya Kapoor: Could we add an opt-in flag for product teams to receive projection diffs? Otherwise LGTM for the core. Please add e2e test that asserts rate-limiting of telemetry export.
Sofia Martinez: Added product opt-in metadata, and extended e2e to assert telemetry export QPS < configured threshold. CI e2e passing locally.
Liam O'Connor: Quick nit: use existing prometheus metric name prefix (telemetry.replay_) to keep queries consistent. Added an approval after the metric rename and small doc tweak.
Aiden Wu: Approved. Priya: Approved. Merging with squash once CI finishes clean run.

release_notes:
Added an offline SLO replay service that provides projected SLO and cost signals (telemetry.replay.attenuation_proxy). New Grafana 'Retro SLO Projections' dashboard. Canary alert rules can optionally consult the projection attenuation signal for temporary suppression during rollouts. See docs/observability/slo-replay.md for runbook and RBAC guidance.
